sections.text: 在微软工作一年后，我决定重新开始写写AI native designer的转型过程，和AI design workflow的变化，希望能链接更多感兴趣的人。
这次聊的话题是因为前段时间参与了一些Generative UI的项目，因此分享一些总结和反思。
看完本文你能获得：
✅ 为什么GenUI重要，明天就可以和同事侃侃而谈
✅ GenUI的形态和行为，设计的重点是什么
✅ 什么Figma不再能设计GenUI，以及我自己的工作流
看完本文你不能获得：
❎ OpenAI的工作机会（但可以增加你获得的概率）
❎ 一只会叫你名字的可爱小猫咪 🐱（但你可以自己vibe coding它）
如何打造一个AI native的GenUI产品呢？其实非常简单👇
正片从这里开始 ～
AI时代，人机界面的体验倒退了
在AI这个时代，我们拥有了足够智能且持续进化的AI系统。讽刺的是，我们的人机交互体验在很多场景反而倒退了——从丰富的图形化界面体验退回到基于文本的对话聊天，能力强大，但表达原始，很多时候信息可读性很低，阅读效率也不高。
AI输出的Text-based界面创造了一种扁平的信息层级，但整段文字的回答非常overwhelming，难以阅读。特别是现在AI也被用在一些任务流的场景中，其实非常低效。用户在大段的文字中寻找相关的信息时，过高的认知负荷和跳跃的重点，会降低用户对AI 的回答的信任感。
GenUI，是AI时代的人机界面
GenUI是由AI实时动态生成的用户界面。
总的来说支持GenUI的AI agent输出的是结构化和可交互的UI，对比当前的大部分Text-based回答：
1. 回答不仅有内容，还有视觉结构和重点
2. 可交互，用户有更高的互动意愿
3. 用户对回答和agent都有更强的信任感
GenUI 的行为
大多数真实世界的AI产品体验可以归为三种界面形态：Chat、Chat+、Chatless。GenUI在不同形态的产品中也有不同的表现。
Chat:
在对话中的交互，对话就是产品。
在这种模式下，GenUI 通常以内嵌形式出现，例如卡片、图表、摘要或工具的结构化区块。比如Open UI提供的开源GenUI能力
Chat+
对话+产品界面共同协作，聊天依然存在，但它只是更大工作区域的一部分。用户通过对话，让AI在可操作的界面中生成GenUI，共同完成任务。比如 Google Stitch在画布种生成UI。
Chatless
界面会在没有任何聊天窗口的情况下自动适配。用户几乎感觉不到“在和 AI 对话”，系统会根据用户的input直接输出新的GenUI更新界面。比如Copilot lab中根据用户的行为自动生成的地图和体验的游戏
GenUI 的行为
有2个影响 GenUI 行为的关键：表达自由度和谁来控制表达
表达自由度（Freedom of Expression）：
决定了系统在视觉和结构上可以让AI “生成到什么程度”。一般来说有3种：
1. 固定组件系统（Low Freedom）：
AI 仅允许调用有限的系统预设组件（比如lists，widget，cards），AI 只能在固定卡片、列表或表单之间选择，不允许结构突破
2. 扩展组件系统（Medium Freedom）：
AI 还是调用有限的系统预设组件，但允许不同组件的拼装，组合，Grouping
3. 开放生成系统（High Freedom）：
AI 可以生成完整的HTML 或free-form布局（比如用design skills让AI自由生成UI）
谁来控制表达（Who Controls the Representation）：
一些场景开发者会定义好应用引用GenUI的规则（比如只能用某 3 种卡片），这种情况下产品规定结构，模型只填数据。
另一些场景会让模型自己决定怎么呈现（如用表格，生成多个卡的Grouping，或输出完整 HTML）。产品不再规定结构，只负责渲染模型输出的内容
大多数现实世界的产品处于中间地带，由应用设定边界，而模型在这些边界内进行自适应。
GenUI 时代，Figma 似乎不再可行
Gen UI的设计成为了一个难题，不像传统的静态UI，GenUI需要测试不同components千变万化的组合。这在Figma中几乎无法完成，因此我们需要打造新的工具，确保上线前就能充分测试GenUI的各种edge cases.
理想的GenUI，和AI可能拼接出的奇怪UI👇
AI Workflow，打造 GenUI 工具
我一直希望让参与设计的 Copilot 能输出内容丰富的UI界面，而不只是text heavy的大段文案。在古法设计时期（1年多前），用Figma手搓很难穷尽所有的组合场景。而现在，只要有Claude code以及产品的Codebase，就可以搭建属于自己的GenUI设计工具。在产品上线之前就能看到自己搭建的GenUI系统在各种场景的表现。
经过调研，我找到一个开源的GenUI库，并理出了实现的技术架构：
• 定义一个GenUI design system
• 和LLM约定好，返回的内容中带有表达GenUI的Tag
• 然后让agent根据规则，将带Tag的返回信息，在浏览器渲染成带有UI的回复内容
我把开源库clone到本地，把库中的GenUI样式调整得尽可能和Copilot相似，然后和Copilot代码库相结合，让我们看看效果！
我询问了一个日本的旅游计划，Copilot 的回答使用了多种GenUI，输出了图文并茂，且可以交互的详细计划👇
对比纯文本的AI回答，GenUI内容结构明显会更有重点，视觉上更有吸引力👇
甚至我输入申请信用卡相关的问题，AI直接生成了我一个可交互的申请流程，可以直接填写提交。
至此，以后要增加新的GenUI 组件和规则，不再需要Figma手搓，只需要向Claude code描述成新的components和规则，甚至让AI自动生成evals（评估系统）测试，就能快速判断新的设计表现是否符合预期。
好啦，虽然还有很多没说完，但是真的要去睡觉了😴 欢迎交流！

sections_en.text: After a year at Microsoft, I decided to start writing again about my transition as an AI-native designer and the evolution of AI design workflows, hoping to connect with more like-minded people.
This time I'm sharing insights from recent Generative UI projects. After reading, you'll gain:
✅ Why GenUI matters — enough to discuss with colleagues tomorrow
✅ GenUI forms and behaviors — what designers should focus on
✅ Why Figma can no longer design GenUI, and my own workflow
What you won't get:
❎ A job at OpenAI (but this might improve your chances)
❎ A cute kitten that calls your name 🐱(but you can vibe-code one yourself)
How to build an AI-native GenUI product? It's actually quite simple 👇
The real content starts here ~
In the AI Era, Human-Computer Interface Experience Has Regressed

In the AI era, we have sufficiently intelligent and continuously evolving AI systems. Ironically, our HCI experience has regressed — from rich graphical interfaces back to text-based chat. Powerful in capability, but primitive in expression, with low readability and poor efficiency.

AI's text-based output creates a flat information hierarchy. Long text responses are overwhelming and hard to read. In task-flow scenarios it's very inefficient. High cognitive load and scattered key points reduce user trust in AI responses.
GenUI: The Human-Computer Interface of the AI Era
GenUI is user interface dynamically generated by AI in real-time.
AI agents supporting GenUI output structured, interactive UI. Compared to current text-based responses:
1. Responses have content WITH visual structure and emphasis
2. Interactive — higher engagement willingness
3. Users have stronger trust in both response and agent
Behaviors of GenUI
Most real-world AI product experiences fall into three interface forms: Chat, Chat+, and Chatless. GenUI manifests differently in each.
Chat:
Interaction within conversation — the chat IS the product.
In this mode, GenUI appears as embedded blocks — cards, charts, summaries, or structured tool outputs. For example, Open UI's open-source GenUI capabilities.
Chat+

Conversation + product interface working together. Chat still exists, but as part of a larger workspace. Users have AI generate GenUI in an actionable canvas. E.g., Google Stitch generating UI in canvas.
Chatless

The interface adapts automatically without any chat window. Users barely feel they're "talking to AI" — the system outputs new GenUI directly based on user input. E.g., Copilot Lab's auto-generated maps and games.
Behaviors of GenUI
Two key factors influence GenUI behavior: Freedom of Expression and Who Controls the Representation.
Freedom of Expression:
Determines how far the system allows AI to "generate" visually and structurally. Three levels:
1. Fixed Component System (Low Freedom):
AI can only call limited preset components (lists, widgets, cards). No structural breakthroughs allowed.
2. Extended Component System (Medium Freedom):
AI still calls preset components but allows assembly, combination, and grouping.
3. Open Generation System (High Freedom):
AI can generate complete HTML or free-form layouts (e.g., using design skills for AI to freely generate UI).
Who Controls the Representation:
In some scenarios, developers define GenUI rules (e.g., only 3 card types). The product dictates structure, the model fills data.
In other scenarios, the model decides presentation (tables, card groupings, or full HTML). The product no longer dictates structure, only renders model output.
Most real-world products fall in between — the application sets boundaries, the model adapts within them.
In the GenUI Era, Figma Is No Longer Viable

Designing GenUI is a challenge. Unlike traditional static UI, GenUI requires testing ever-changing component combinations. Nearly impossible in Figma — we need new tools to test edge cases before launch.
Ideal GenUI vs. the weird UI that AI might assemble 👇
AI Workflow: Building GenUI Tools

I've always wanted Copilot to output rich UI, not just text-heavy paragraphs. In the old-school design era (1+ year ago), Figma couldn't cover all scenarios. Now with Claude Code and the product codebase, you can build your own GenUI design tools and preview across scenarios before launch.
After research, I found an open-source GenUI library and mapped out the technical architecture:
• Define a GenUI design system
• Agree with the LLM on a protocol where responses include GenUI tags
• Then have the agent render tagged responses as UI components in the browser based on the rules
I cloned the library locally, adjusted GenUI styles to match Copilot, then combined with the Copilot codebase. Let's see the results!
I asked for a Japan travel plan. Copilot used multiple GenUI components, outputting a detailed interactive plan with rich media 👇
Compared to pure text AI responses, GenUI clearly has better structure, focal points, and visual appeal 👇
I even asked about credit card applications — the AI generated an interactive application flow I could fill out and submit directly.
From now on, adding new GenUI components no longer requires Figma. Just describe new components to Claude Code, even have AI auto-generate evals to validate designs.
Alright, there's still much more to say, but I really need to sleep 😴 Feel free to reach out!

• 产品围绕AI能力为核心设计
• 产品能力会随着AI模型能力提升而变得更强
• 为Agent使用设计
在后续迭代中，我还希望我的AI产品：
• AI行为从简单规则涌现，少写规则，多写原则
• 将产品拆分到最小单元，定义这些基本单元，剩下的一切都是它们的组合
• 了解模型能力的边界，在边界内通过harness达到更好的产品效果
• AI 会犯错，产品要优雅处理不确定性
我觉得做AI产品和钓鱼很像（对的我也喜欢钓鱼），来得太早或太晚都没有收获（模型能力没达到，或已被模型能力覆盖），而是要判断潮汐趋势，在对的timing下竿。
做AI产品，要提前判断模型能力的发展，让产品能在模型能力的边界处发光。

sections_en.text: When I started designing this personal website, I wanted the website itself to be an AI-native product—one that reflects my own principles for AI-native product design.
I believe an AI-native product should follow these principles:
• The product is designed around AI capabilities as its core.
• The product becomes more powerful as AI models improve.
• The product is designed not only for humans, but also for agents.
In future iterations, I want this AI product to further embrace the following ideas:
• AI behavior should emerge from simple principles rather than complex rules. Write fewer rules, define better principles.
• Break the product down into its smallest building blocks, clearly define those primitives, and let everything else emerge from their combinations.
• Understand the boundaries of model capabilities, and use harnesses and system design to maximize product quality within those boundaries.
• AI will make mistakes. Products should handle uncertainty gracefully rather than pretending certainty.

I think building AI products is like fishing (yes, I also love fishing) — arriving too early or too late yields nothing (model capabilities haven't reached the threshold, or have already surpassed it). The key is to anticipate where the boundary will be
Building AI products requires anticipating the development of model capabilities, so the product can shine right at the frontier of what's possible.

sections.text: 脱口秀是我一生的热爱。把生活的酸甜苦辣变成段子搬上舞台的过程，已经成为我生活中不可分割的一部分。我发现脱口秀和设计之间有很多共通之处：

• 两者都需要不断迭代和打磨素材
• 两者都是把日常痛点转化为有意义的东西——设计将其变为解决方案，喜剧将其变为笑声
• 开放麦本质上就是一种用户测试：你听取观众反馈，迭代，再改进
• 喜剧和设计都需要品味——能注意到大多数人忽略但又能引起共鸣的东西
喜剧不仅提升了我的幽默感，也锻炼了我的演讲和沟通能力。在工作中用讲故事的方式推动想法，更容易获得认同。
从2023年开始，我一直在用英文做脱口秀，跟随 Norah 和 Dave 等知名喜剧演员学习技巧。我的素材通常围绕文化差异、科技行业的趣事、以及个人生活的日常展开。
虽然中国的英文脱口秀场景相对小众，但你偶尔可以在上海和北京的开放麦活动中看到我。

sections_en.text: Stand-up comedy is a lifelong passion of mine. The process of turning life's highs and lows into jokes and performing them on stage has become an integral part of my life. Comedy and design have many things in common.
• Both require a sharp eye for observing everyday life.
• Both involve constant iteration and refinement of ideas and materials.
• Both turn everyday pain points into something meaningful — design turns them into solutions, comedy turns them into punchlines.
• An open mic is essentially a form of user testing: you listen to audience feedback, iterate, and improve. Sometimes the feedback is so bad that the material never makes it to production 🤣
• Both comedy and design require taste—the ability to notice things that most people overlook but somehow feel off. This sensitivity is a talent shared by great comedians and great designers alike.

Comedy not only enhances my sense of humor but also improves my public speaking and communication skills. It’s a great way to channel negative emotions into something positive, helping me stay optimistic. Bad day? Great-time to write a new joke!
Since 2023, I’ve been doing stand-up in English, learning from well-known comedians like Norah and Davy, popular faces on Rock & Roast.
Although the English stand-up scene in China is relatively niche, you can catch my performances at some international comedy clubs.

sections_en.text: This project was a school assignment from nearly 10 years ago, but I still love it. Because it reminds me — I'm a builder. Whether or not we're in the AI era, making things come to life excites me!

Fire is the most primitive medium of interaction between humans and light. People cup their hands to protect a candle flame, blow to extinguish it, and even a gentle breeze can change its direction. The invention of electric light made human-light interaction more direct. This project attempts to redesign electric lighting using the interactive language of fire and flame.
I used different sensors to let the product perceive surrounding temperature, light, and atmospheric pressure, then used an Arduino to control the output based on these inputs.

I wanted this product to be a warm piece of art rather than a tech-heavy electronic device. So I made my own silicone molds and used cement as the material, going through several iterations of different forms.
This is my favorite form among them. Users can light it with a match, interact with it by hand, and blow it out like a birthday candle!

article.title_en: Product Design Thoughts on DeepSeek Harness
article.author: 赖健勋 Jesse
notion_zh: DeepSeek Harness 发布以后，基于 “Everything is a plugin” 的理念，我在想如果我是它的产品设计师，会如何设计？我的设计认为设计策略是：把界面拆解成基础原子，一切复杂界面都由基础原子组成，通过定义原子间的组合规则，实现灵活而多变的系统。

notion_zh.highlight_text: 把界面拆解成基础原子，一切复杂界面都由基础原子组成，通过定义原子间的组合规则，实现灵活而多变的系统。

notion_zh: 在过去几年的职业生涯中，我正好就在做这件事：利用简单的基本元素，搭建多变的复杂系统。

notion_zh.highlight_text: 利用简单的基本元素，搭建多变的复杂系统。

notion_zh: 这会让产品设计的重心，从设计一个 Agent，变成设计一个可复用、可组合的创造系统。产品设计师需要深度参与这个系统的 3 个阶段：

1. 打磨默认体验
2. 激发创造活力
3. 维护社区生态
最终让不同阶段的用户都容易理解、易于创造、乐于开源。
通过有良好体验的产品，降低普通用户使用门槛，让用户长期留在 DeepSeek Harness 生态内。
挑战：灵活的插件带来了更高复杂度
“Everything is a plugin” 意味着用户界面也需要应对更多不断变化的插件带来的复杂度。这个问题会导致：产品界面随着插件体系越来越臃肿和不可控，最终成为 Agent 进化的瓶颈。
设计策略：把复杂界面分解为原子结构
“形式追随功能”。通过技术特点和关键挑战，推导设计策略。
设计理念——Everything is an atom
从 Notion 文档的设计理念得到启发，Notion 的基础原子是“Block”。不论多复杂的 Notion 页面，都是由最基础的 Block 组成，也有点像 Web 开发的“盒模型”。Notion 在早期定义清楚了原子结构 Block 的行为和边界，系统的复杂度就变得可以被管理。
那么 Agent 产品的基础元素是什么呢？我的第一个答案是“Session”。
回想一下主流 Coding Agent 的一切。每一个 Query、每个任务、每个项目，都是由多个 Sessions 组成的。还能再拆分吗？Session 还能被拆分为 Query 和 Response，但它们两个单拿出来不足以组成完整体验。
不论多复杂的 Agent 界面，都可以由可复用、可组合的原子单位 Session 组成，实现自由的组合布局，就像插件一样。原子种类是有限的，而组合出的界面是无限的。
我用这个设计理念改造了 DeepSeek Harness。
用户可以在一个窗口中同时打开多个 Session，并行修改同一个项目。甚至 Agent 在运行中也可以自主打开或关闭多个 Session 或 Sub-agent，过程中用户可以随时观察并介入。
甚至可以将 Session 拖到 Agent 外作为独立窗口，独立窗口互相之间也可以灵活拼接，就像插件一样。用户在使用多个显示器时就非常方便了。
导航区也是可拆卸的灵活结构，与 Session 进行不同位置的组合，可以展示出不同的形态，以适应用户个性化需求。
主流 Coding Agent 最大的体验问题之一，是使用场景和 Context 分离。一个典型场景是：用户在使用自己的办公软件或浏览器时，把这些 App 中的 Context 多次来回复制粘贴到 Coding Agent；Coding Agent 处理完以后，再把结果复制回 App 中，注意力很分散。
于是我给 Agent 设计了一个更长的“手”——一个随时可以在使用场景中唤起的手，帮用户把 Context 放到 Agent 里。
这只手可以在任何应用中唤起，你只管输入指令，不用说 Context，它都知道。
从跨国沟通时的消息润色和翻译：
写文档时，基于文档内容进行配图：
看到 GitHub 中的开源项目，可以直接开发：
长程任务的挑战——Human in the loop
用户会通过思维链判断 Agent 推理过程是否符合预期。但思维链的一个问题是：对普通用户来说看不懂，对专业用户来说又不够细。因此，对不同层次的用户，灵活展示思维链的表达很重要。
长达数小时的大型任务越来越多，失败的成本也越大。一个常见场景是：回顾思维链时，发现最后几步推理错误，但却要重新执行整个任务，大量时间和 Token 都被浪费了。
针对这个问题，我的设计让用户在任务执行中或完成后，从思维链的任意节点开始“重新推理”。“重新推理”会保留该节点之前的推理过程和产出，放弃该节点之后的所有内容，并基于用户的补充信息重新推理，提升任务完成效率，减少 Token 浪费。
阶段 2：创造途径——激发开发者的创造力
针对有定制化需求的开发者，帮助他们了解和使用 DeepSeek Harness 灵活的插件理念。这时设计师不是设计某一个产品，而是像乐高积木设计师一样，将组成产品的基础原子和搭建方法交给玩家，激发社区玩家的创造力。
从目前社区的用户反馈中，我发现了这个阶段在产品设计上的挑战：用户 Vibe 出来的插件在交互模式和 UI 上都不一致，反而破坏了核心体验。
我通过对 VS Code 开源生态治理方式的调研，获得了一些启发。VS Code 本质上是一个可扩展编辑器平台，很多能力都通过 Extension API 挂进去，很多核心功能本身也是以 Extension 方式实现的。核心有 3 层：

• Extension API：定义能力可以插入哪里。
• Marketplace：分发与管理。
• UX Guidelines：告诉用户交互行为如何尽量“像 VS Code”。
在这个阶段，产品设计师可以将内部使用的“设计资产”产品化，包括：

• 开放、可复用、可组合的“积木系统”（Design Library／Tokens）。
• 帮助开发者进行创作的“搭建规则”（UX Guidelines）。
• 开发者 Onboarding 体验：开发者第一次制作插件的体验。
让开发者们不用再担心 Vibe Coding 的交互体验，把更多精力放在插件的核心价值上，提升社区的创新效率，帮助社区开发者搭建出体验优秀的插件。
随着社区壮大，我们需要让优质插件被更多人看到和使用，同时保持用户创造的积极性。从目前社区的用户反馈中，我发现了这个阶段在产品设计上的挑战：好的插件淹没在插件市场中，难以被发现。
我调研了游戏平台 Steam 开源生态的治理方式，发现 Steam 创意工坊本质上是一个 UGC 分发系统。玩家或创作者可以上传模组、地图、物品、外观等游戏内容，其他玩家订阅、下载和更新。它有两种模式：

• Ready-to-use Workshop：（1）任何人都能上传；（2）玩家可以直接下载使用。
• Curated Workshop：（1）开发者逐个审批；（2）社区内容先进入投票或筛选队列。
这个阶段在产品设计上可以：

• 参与构建一个完善而繁荣的社区生态，建设插件市场和插件筛选机制。
• 从社区创新中发现优化官方产品的思路。
更好的用户体验能帮助 DeepSeek Harness 获得更多基础用户，这些基础用户可以逐渐转化成生态内的创作者；最终繁荣生态中的许多好想法，又可以反哺基础用户体验的提升。
综上，我觉得 DeepSeek Harness 团队需要的不只是懂某一领域、拥有单一经验的设计专家，而是在产品发展的各个阶段，对不同领域都有了解、强调系统性思维的通才。我觉得我的过往经历和技能，与 DeepSeek Harness 团队构建开放、可复用、可组合的基础设施和开发者生态的目标非常契合：

（1）Agent 设计：Coding Agent 的设计和开发经历让我充分了解 Agent 产品设计。
（2）处理复杂：微软的 GenUI 及 Copilot 设计系统项目，让我理解复杂系统如何由简单原子组成。
（3）AI Native：搭建数十个 AI 产品和工作流，让我对 AI Native 研发流程拥有足够经验和热情。
（4）全球化：Copilot 产品设计经历，让我具备面向全球数亿用户打磨产品品质、帮助产品走向全球市场的经验。
（5）涉猎广泛：交互体验、视觉创意、原型开发、用户调研，甚至插画等综合能力。
（6）好奇心：生活中我对写作和喜剧的热情，以及 AI Native 的创作流程（构思—实践—评估），让我积累了 Agent 任务质量评估经验，也让我在 AI 时代依然保持好奇。
notion_en: After DeepSeek Harness launched, the idea that “Everything is a plugin” made me ask: if I were its product designer, how would I design it? My design strategy is to decompose the interface into foundational atoms, build every complex interface from those atoms, and define composition rules between atoms to create a flexible, evolving system.

notion_en.highlight_text: decompose the interface into foundational atoms, build every complex interface from those atoms, and define composition rules between atoms to create a flexible, evolving system.

notion_en: Throughout the past few years of my career, this is exactly what I have been doing: using simple building blocks to construct varied, complex systems.

notion_en.highlight_text: using simple building blocks to construct varied, complex systems.

notion_en: This shifts product design from designing one agent to designing a reusable, composable creation system. Product designers need to participate deeply in three stages of that system:

1. Refine the default experience
2. Unlock creative energy
3. Steward the community ecosystem
The goal is to make the system easy to understand, easy to create with, and rewarding to contribute to for users at every stage.
A well-designed product lowers the barrier for mainstream users and keeps them within the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem over time.
Challenge: Flexible Plugins Create More Complexity

“Everything is a plugin” means the interface must handle the complexity created by an ever-changing set of plugins. Left unresolved, the interface becomes increasingly bloated and uncontrollable as the plugin system grows, eventually becoming a bottleneck for the agent’s evolution.
Design Strategy: Decompose Complex Interfaces into Atomic Structures
Form follows function. The design strategy should be derived from the technology’s defining characteristics and its key challenges.
Design Principle — Everything Is an Atom

I drew inspiration from Notion’s design philosophy. Its foundational atom is the Block: no matter how complex a Notion page becomes, it is assembled from basic Blocks, much like the box model on the web. By defining the behavior and boundaries of Blocks early, Notion made system complexity manageable.
So what is the foundational element of an agent product? My first answer is the Session.

Think about mainstream coding agents: every query, task, and project consists of multiple Sessions. Can we break one down further? A Session can be split into a Query and a Response, but neither can form a complete experience on its own.

Any agent interface, no matter how complex, can be composed from reusable, composable Session atoms and arranged freely, just like plugins. The types of atoms are finite, but the interfaces they can compose are infinite.
I used this design principle to reimagine DeepSeek Harness.

Users can open multiple Sessions in one window and modify the same project in parallel. An Agent can even open or close multiple Sessions or Sub-agents autonomously while it runs, with users free to observe or intervene at any time.
A Session can also be dragged outside the agent into its own window. Independent windows can still snap together flexibly like plugins, which is especially useful across multiple displays.
Navigation can also be a detachable, flexible structure that combines with Sessions in different positions and forms to match personal needs.

One of the biggest experience problems in today’s coding agents is the separation between the work surface and its context. Users work in office apps or browsers, repeatedly copy context into a coding agent, and then move the result back into the original app, fragmenting their attention.
So I designed a longer “hand” for the agent—one that can be invoked from any work surface and bring the surrounding context into the agent.
This hand can be invoked from any application. You provide the instruction without describing the context; the agent already knows it.
It can polish and translate messages during cross-border communication:
While writing a document, it can create visuals from the document’s content:
When you discover an open-source project on GitHub, it can move directly into development:
The Challenge of Long-Running Tasks — Human in the Loop
1) Readability of the Chain of Thought

Users rely on the chain of thought to judge whether the Agent is reasoning as expected. General users may not understand it, while experts may find it insufficiently detailed. The expression of the chain of thought therefore needs to adapt flexibly to different levels of users.

Multi-hour tasks are becoming more common, and the cost of failure is growing. A familiar pattern is discovering that only the final reasoning steps were wrong, yet having to rerun the entire task and waste substantial time and tokens.

My design lets users restart reasoning from any point in the chain, during or after execution. It preserves the reasoning and outputs before that point, discards everything after it, and reasons again from the user’s additional information—improving completion efficiency and reducing token waste.

For developers with customization needs, the product should help them understand and use DeepSeek Harness’s flexible plugin philosophy. The designer is no longer designing a single product; like a LEGO designer, they give players the foundational atoms and building methods that unlock community creativity.
Current community feedback reveals a product-design challenge at this stage: vibe-coded plugins use inconsistent interaction patterns and UI, damaging the core experience.

Research into the governance of the VS Code open-source ecosystem offers a useful model. VS Code is an extensible editor platform: many capabilities plug in through Extension APIs, and many core capabilities are themselves implemented as extensions. It has three layers:

• Extension API: defines where capabilities can plug in.
• Marketplace: handles distribution and management.
• UX Guidelines: help interaction patterns continue to feel like VS Code.
At this stage, product designers can turn internal design assets into products, including:

• An open, reusable, composable building system (Design Library and Tokens).
• Building rules that help developers create (UX Guidelines).

设计理念——Everything is an atom
我从 Notion 文档的设计理念中得到启发。Notion 的基础原子是“Block”：无论多复杂的 Notion 页面，都是由最基础的 Block 组成，也有点像 Web 开发中的“盒模型”。Notion 在早期定义清楚了原子结构 Block 的行为和边界，系统的复杂度就变得可以被管理。

sections_latest.text: 那么 Agent 产品的基础元素是什么？我的第一个答案是“Session”。
回想主流 Coding Agent 的一切：每一个 Query、每个任务、每个项目，都是由多个 Sessions 组成的。还能再拆分吗？Session 还能被拆分为 Query 和 Response，但它们单独拿出来不足以组成完整体验。

sections_latest.text: 那么，不论多复杂的 Agent 界面，都可以由可复用、可组合的原子单位 Session 组成，实现像插件一样自由的组合布局。原子种类是有限的，而组合出的界面是无限的。
比如，用户可以在一个界面中同时打开多个 Session，并行修改同一个项目。这也让 Agent 在运行中可以自主开启多个 Session 或 Sub-agent 执行任务，完成后再退出；整个过程中，用户都可以随时观察并介入。
甚至可以将 Session 拖到 Agent 外作为独立窗口；它们彼此之间也可以像插件一样灵活拼接，特别适合使用多个显示器的场景。
导航区也是可拆卸的灵活结构，可以与 Session 在不同位置组合，展示出不同形态，以适应用户的个性化需求。
使用场景和 Agent 分离问题
目前主流 Coding Agent 最大的问题，仍然是使用场景和 Context 分离。典型场景是：用户在办公软件或浏览器中工作，把要处理的 Context 多次来回复制粘贴到 Coding Agent；处理完成后，再把结果放回原来的使用场景，浪费了很多注意力。

思维链对长程任务至关重要，用户会据此判断 Agent 的推理过程是否符合预期。它的一个挑战是：普通用户看不懂，而专业用户又觉得不够细。这两种情况都无法帮助各自用户做出有效判断。因此，一个能够根据不同用户层次变化的、灵活的思维链非常重要。

sections_en_latest.text: Fortunately, this is exactly what I have been doing throughout the past few years of my career: using simple building blocks to construct varied, complex systems.

This shifts product design from designing one agent to designing a reusable, composable creation system. Product designers should deeply shape and refine its onboarding experience, paths to creation, and ecosystem stewardship, so people at every stage can understand it, create with it, and contribute openly.
Stage 1: Onboarding — Decompose Complex Interfaces into Atomic Structures

A strong onboarding experience comes from polished first-party products that lower the barrier for the broadest audience and keep users within the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem. Like a LEGO set, users can choose the right combination of pieces for each task.

• Audience: mainstream users and people encountering DeepSeek Harness for the first time.
• Product goal: work out of the box and provide the best possible coding experience by default.

sections_en_latest.text: Stage 1 Challenge — Flexible Plugins Create Complexity

“Everything is a plugin” also means the interface must absorb greater complexity. How can it adapt to plugins that continuously change for both users and agents? If this remains unresolved, the product will become increasingly bloated as the plugin system grows, eventually limiting its evolution.
Stage 1 Design Strategy — Atomic Design

sections_en_latest.alt: From a flexible plugin system to an atomic design strategy

sections_en_latest.text: I believe form follows function, so a plugin system needs a corresponding product-design strategy. With that question in mind, I redesigned and open-sourced a DeepSeek Harness client and developed new solutions for major coding-agent challenges: long-running tasks, context, and chains of thought.
Design Principle — Everything Is an Atom

I drew inspiration from Notion’s design philosophy. Its foundational atom is the Block: no matter how complex a Notion page becomes, it is assembled from basic Blocks, much like the box model on the web. By defining the behavior and boundaries of Blocks early, Notion made system complexity manageable.

sections_en_latest.alt: How Notion Blocks compose into pages

sections_en_latest.text: So what is the foundational element of an agent product? My first answer is the Session.

Think about mainstream coding agents: every query, task, and project consists of multiple Sessions. Can we break one down further? A Session can be split into a Query and a Response, but neither can form a complete experience on its own.

sections_en_latest.caption: A Session is the smallest complete unit of an agent.
sections_en_latest.alt: Session as an atomic agent unit

sections_en_latest.text: Any agent interface, no matter how complex, can therefore be composed from reusable Session atoms and arranged freely, just like plugins. The types of atoms are finite, but the interfaces they can compose are infinite.

For example, users can open multiple Sessions in one interface and modify the same project in parallel. This also lets an Agent autonomously launch multiple Sessions or Sub-agents while it runs, close them when their work is done, and keep users free to observe or intervene at any time.
A Session can even be dragged outside the agent into its own window. Sessions can still snap together flexibly like plugins, which is especially useful across multiple displays.
Navigation can also be a detachable, flexible structure that combines with Sessions in different positions and forms to match personal needs.
Separating the Work Surface from the Agent

A major problem with today’s coding agents is still the separation between the work surface and its context. Users work in office apps or browsers, repeatedly copy context into a coding agent, and then move the result back into the original app, wasting a great deal of attention.

sections_en_latest.text: Inspired by the Mac Shortcuts app, I designed a longer “hand” for the agent—one that can be invoked from any work surface and pull the surrounding context directly into the agent.
It is a shortcut that can be invoked from any application. You provide the instruction without manually adding tedious context; the agent can already see it.
It can begin with something simple, such as polishing and translating Teams messages during cross-border collaboration:
While writing a document, it can create visuals from the existing content:
When you discover an interesting open-source project on GitHub, it can move directly into development:

1) Readability of the chain of thought

Chains of thought are crucial in long-running tasks because users rely on them to judge whether the agent is reasoning as expected. One challenge is that the reasoning may be incomprehensible to general users yet insufficiently detailed for experts. Neither group can make an effective judgment. A flexible chain of thought that adapts to the user’s level is therefore essential.
2) Intent drift in long-running tasks

As multi-hour tasks become more common, each failure becomes harder to absorb. Sometimes only the final reasoning steps are wrong, yet the entire task must be rerun, wasting substantial time and tokens.

My design lets users restart reasoning from any point in the chain, during or after execution. It preserves the reasoning and outputs before that point, discards everything after it, and reasons again from the user’s feedback.

The designer is no longer designing a single product; like a LEGO designer, they give players the foundational atoms and building methods that unlock community creativity.

• Audience: advanced users and developers with custom needs.

这个思路受到 Notion Block 的启发：千变万化的页面都由 Block 组成，也像 Web 开发中的盒模型。只要定义清楚基础元素的行为和边界，系统复杂度就可以被管理。
那么 Agent 产品的基础元素是什么？我目前的答案是 Session。每个 query、任务和项目都由多个 sessions 组成；Query 与 Response 还能继续拆分，但它们单独并不足以组成完整体验。
用户可以基于原子自由调整界面布局，Agent 也可以像使用插件一样自行组合。有限的原子，可以拼出无限的界面：导航能换边，一个界面能容纳多个 sessions，也能把 session 独立成新窗口。
如果模型是大脑，Agent 就是灵活的手。因此我用“手”作为 Agent 的视觉意象；复杂的图标和插画，也同样由更基础、可复用、可组合的原子拼接而成。
让 Agent 更靠近 Context
当前 Coding Agent 的典型问题，是使用场景与 Context 分离：用户在办公软件或浏览器里工作，却要把上下文反复复制到 Coding Agent，处理完成后再把结果搬回原来的场景。
受到 macOS 快捷指令的启发，我给 Agent 设计了一只更长的“手”——一个可在任何应用中唤起的快捷入口。用户只管输入指令，不必手动补齐繁琐的 Context，Agent 就能看到当前场景。
它可以在 Teams 中润色和翻译跨国协作消息，在 Notion 写作时基于已有内容配图，也可以看到 GitHub 上感兴趣的项目后直接进入开发。
继续探索的 Agent 体验
• 长程任务中的意图漂移，以及任务结束后的 Steer from here
• 思维链专业度调节与时序贡献度分配
• 项目内记忆与多模型调度，在节省 tokens 的同时保持上下文连续
• 在对话内直接调用 Harness 页面
对于硬核 builder、开源开发者和希望重新定义 Agent 工作方式的人，还需要开放 loop、session、memory、tool、UI surface、desktop bridge 等可插拔层，并提供清晰的扩展表面、调试工具、文档、沙箱、示例和回滚机制。最后，让人真正能造。
阶段 2：创造途径——激发开发者的创造力
面向有定制需求的进阶用户和开发者，设计师不再只设计某个产品，而要像乐高积木设计师一样，把组成产品的基础原子和搭建方法交给玩家，帮助他们创造高质量插件和更深入的改造。
目前的挑战是：优秀插件容易淹没在市场中；不同开发者 Vibe 出来的交互和 UI 缺乏一致性，反而会破坏核心体验。
VS Code 的开源生态提供了三层启发：Extension API 定义能力插入点，Marketplace 负责分发与管理，UX Guidelines 帮助扩展保持一致的平台心智。
因此，产品设计师可以把内部设计资产产品化：开放可组合的 Design Library 与 Tokens、面向插件的 UX Guidelines，以及插件模板和案例教学。开发者可以把精力集中到插件的核心价值上，而不是重复解决基础交互问题。
阶段 3：生态维护
随着社区壮大，需要让优质插件被更多人发现和使用，同时保持创作者的积极性。Steam 创意工坊提供了两种治理方式：任何人都能发布、用户直接订阅的 Ready-to-use Workshop，以及由开发者审批、社区先投票筛选的 Curated Workshop。
这个阶段的设计工作，是参与构建繁荣且可持续的社区生态，包括插件市场、发现机制、质量筛选与体验评估框架。评估可以关注：是否容易理解、是否符合平台心智、是否清楚暴露权限与风险、是否破坏任务流、能否与其他插件共存，以及是否具备合理的 fallback、empty state 和 error state。
我还能做什么
更好的基础体验会带来更多用户，其中一部分会成长为生态创作者；繁荣生态中的优秀想法，又会反哺基础体验。这形成了“留在生态—制作插件—深入创作—提升体验”的飞轮。
我与这个目标的契合点包括：Coding Agent 的设计与开发经历；微软多个 GenUI 项目与 Copilot 设计系统经验；数十个 Vibe Coding 产品和 AI 工作流实践；以及写作与喜剧带来的创作、实践和评估能力。

sections_en.text: After DeepSeek Harness launched, I experimented extensively, publishing a client and several plugins. Building on the idea that “Everything is a plugin,” I believe its product strategy should decompose interfaces into foundational atoms, then use clear composition rules to create a flexible, evolving system.

For the past few years, I have been working on the same question: how can simple building blocks create many complex systems? The focus of product design shifts from making one useful agent to designing a reusable, composable creation system.
Product designers should help shape onboarding, paths to creation, and ecosystem stewardship, so people at every stage can understand the system, create with it, and contribute back.
Stage 1: Onboarding — Decompose Complex Interfaces into Atoms

A strong onboarding experience begins with polished first-party products. They lower the barrier for new users, provide an excellent coding experience out of the box, and work like LEGO sets: people choose the right combination of pieces for each task.

“Everything is a plugin” also means the UI must absorb constantly changing user and agent needs. Without a clearly defined foundation, the interface will become increasingly bloated as the plugin ecosystem grows, eventually limiting the product itself.
With these questions in mind, I redesigned and open-sourced a DeepSeek Harness client, while exploring new approaches to long-running tasks, context, and chains of thought in coding agents.
Design Principle: Everything Is an Atom

The idea is inspired by Notion blocks: infinitely varied pages are built from a small set of blocks, much like the box model on the web. Once the behavior and boundaries of those primitives are clear, system complexity becomes manageable.

What is the foundational atom of an agent product? My current answer is the session. Every query, task, and project is made of sessions. Queries and responses can be split further, but neither can form a complete experience alone.

Users can rearrange the interface from these atoms, and agents can compose them just like plugins. A finite set of atoms can produce infinite interfaces: navigation can move, several sessions can share one surface, and any session can become its own window.

If the model is the brain, the agent is a flexible hand. That is why the visual language uses a hand—and why even complex icons and illustrations can themselves be assembled from smaller reusable atoms.
Bring the Agent Closer to Context

A core problem with today's coding agents is the separation between the work surface and its context. People work in office apps or browsers, repeatedly copy information into the agent, and then move the result back into the original app.

Inspired by macOS Shortcuts, I designed a longer “hand” for the agent: an entry point that can be invoked from any app. The user provides the intent while the agent can already see the surrounding context.
It can polish and translate cross-border Teams messages, create visuals from an existing Notion draft, or move directly from discovering an interesting GitHub project into development.
Further Agent Experience Explorations
• Intent drift in long-running tasks, including “Steer from here” after completion
• Adjusting the expertise level of reasoning and assigning contribution across time
• Project memory and multi-model orchestration that preserve continuity while saving tokens
• Calling Harness pages directly inside a conversation

For power builders, open-source developers, and people redefining agent workflows, the system should also expose pluggable layers such as the loop, session, memory, tools, UI surfaces, and desktop bridge—backed by clear extension points, debugging tools, documentation, sandboxes, examples, and rollback. Ultimately, people should be able to build.
Stage 2: Creation — Inspire Developers

For advanced users and developers with custom needs, the designer no longer designs a single product. Like a LEGO designer, they provide the foundational pieces and building methods that help the community create high-quality plugins and deeper modifications.
Two challenges already stand out: great plugins are easily buried in the marketplace, while inconsistent interaction patterns and UI from vibe-coded plugins can damage the core experience.

The VS Code ecosystem offers a useful three-layer model: Extension APIs define where capabilities plug in, the Marketplace handles distribution and management, and UX Guidelines help extensions feel consistent with the platform.

Design teams can productize their internal assets as an open, composable Design Library and token system, plugin UX guidelines, templates, and practical examples. Developers can then focus on the unique value of their plugins instead of repeatedly solving basic interaction problems.
Stage 3: Ecosystem Stewardship

As the community grows, strong plugins need to become easier to discover without weakening creators' motivation. Steam Workshop suggests two governance modes: a ready-to-use model where anyone can publish and users subscribe directly, and a curated model where submissions pass through review and community selection.

Design work at this stage means building a healthy plugin marketplace, discovery and curation mechanisms, and an experience-quality framework. That framework can ask whether a plugin is understandable, fits the platform's mental model, exposes permissions and risks, protects task flow, coexists with other plugins, and provides sensible fallback, empty, and error states.
What I Can Contribute

A better core experience brings in more users; some become ecosystem creators; the best ideas from that ecosystem then improve the core experience. This creates a flywheel from adoption, to plugin creation, to deeper invention, and back to a better product.

My fit with this goal comes from designing and building coding agents; working across GenUI projects and the Copilot design system at Microsoft; creating dozens of vibe-coded products and AI workflows; and practicing the cycle of creation, performance, and evaluation through writing and comedy.
